name: Cosmic Robotics Cosmic-1A
specialisedFor: utility-scale solar construction: lifting PV modules and placing them on tracker racking
summary: Fully electric eight-wheeled field robot with a KUKA six-axis arm and vision system that picks solar modules and places them on the racking, while workers fasten them. Built by US start-up Cosmic Robotics and used by the contractor Sunstall on US solar projects.

germany.statusNote: No German or EU sales route found. Cosmic Robotics (US) has a quote request on its website and works through certified US operators such as SunRobi, the robotics division of Sunstall; all deployments named are in the United States.

specs.label: Placement accuracy
specs.quote: The robot places the solar panels onto the racking with ±1mm precision.

specs.label: Module weight handled
specs.conditions: with the arm fully extended; about 36 kg
specs.quote: the robot had to be able to handle the 80-pound payload, even with the arm fully extended

specs.label: Robot arm
specs.quote: The company landed on the KR IONTEC robot arm

specs.label: Base
specs.quote: The Cosmic 1A robot is an eight wheeled autonomous platform with a 6-axis industrial robot on the top for panel handling.

specs.label: Drive
specs.quote: The fully electric robot incorporates a rugged all-terrain vehicle platform and a large KUKA robot arm

specs.label: Labour productivity
specs.quote: Cosmic-1 has now achieved 2x labor productivity compared to manual methods for terrestrial solar farm construction.

notes: armPayloadKg is the 80 lb module weight from the KUKA case study converted to kg, not a rated arm payload.
Works in heat, rain and dust; the Foundry arm version has an extended temperature range and pressurised joints (KUKA).
Workers still set up the racking and fasten the modules; a fastening tool is planned.
The maker now calls the system Cosmic-1.

images.alt: Cosmic-1A robot carrying a solar module in a solar field

evidence.task: Lifts and places PV modules on racking on utility-scale solar projects, replacing the lifting work of a five-person crew
evidence.where: Sunstall projects, United States; further installations planned in Colorado and California
evidence.note: Customer case study published by KUKA.

evidence.task: SunRobi certified as first Cosmic operator after multiple deployments on live solar projects

sources.title: Robotic Automation for Utility-Scale Solar Installation (Sunstall and Cosmic Robotics case study)
SunRobi is first certified operator of Cosmic Robotics autonomous solar installation systems (3 February 2026)
